content: Release your grip on past regrets; water that has flowed past the mill cannot turn the wheel again.
author: Zhuangzi
explanation: In The Book of Zhuangzi, Chapter 14, Zhuangzi illustrates how releasing calculated intellectual striving allows the mind to enter the effortless rhythm of the Dao. When we cease imposing rigid expectations on life, our spirit discovers spontaneous freedom and tranquility.
practicalInsight: Approach today's agenda not as a rigid battlefield to conquer, but as a fluid river to navigate with playful presence.
reflectionPrompt: What rigid expectation can you dissolve today to make room for spontaneous joy and natural harmony?
